questions.question: If (X)/(3) = (Y)/(5) = (Z)/(9), then what is the ratio X : Y : Z?
questions.solution:
**Concept:**

If (x/a) = (y/b) = (z/c), then x : y : z = a : b : c

**Calculation:**

(X)/(3) = (Y)/(5) = (Z)/(9) = K

⇒ X = 3K, Y = 5K, Z = 9K

∴ Here, x : y : z = 3 : 5 : 9

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**X/Y = 3/5, Y/Z = 5/9 

⇒ X : Y = 3 : 5

⇒ Y : Z = 5 : 9 

If Y same, then Y = 5

Ratio is 3 : 5 : 9

questions.question: Height of a right circular cylinder is 12 cm. If the radius of its base 21 cm, then what will be the curved surface area of the cylinder?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Height of a right circular cylinder = 12 cm

Radius of its base = 21 cm

**Formula used:**

Curved surface area of cylinder = 2πrh (where r is the radius of base and h is the height of the cylinder)

**Calculation:**

Curved surface area of cylinder = 2 × (22/7) × 21 × 12

⇒ 1584 cm²

questions.question: A sum of ₹14000 is lent at compound interest (interest is compounded annually) for 3 years. If the rate of interest is 10%, then what will be the compound interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal amount, P = 14000

Number of years, N = 3

Rate of interest, R = 10%

**Formula used:**

Total amount, A = P × (1 + (R/100))N

C.I = Total amount – Principal amount

**Calculation:**

Total amount, A = 14000 × (1 + (10/100))³

⇒ A = 18634

∴ C.I = 18634 – 14000 = 4634

questions.question: The area of a square and a rectangle are equal. The length of the rectangle is greater than the side of square by 9 cm and its breadth is less than the side of square by 6 cm. What will be the perimeter of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Let 'a' be the side of square, l be the length and b be the breadth of the rectangle

The area of a square and a rectangle are equal ⇒ a² = l × b

The length of the rectangle is greater than the side of square by 9 cm and its breadth is less than the side of square by 6 cm

⇒ l = a + 9

⇒ b = a – 6

**Formula used:**

Area of Square = side²

Area of Rectangle = length × breadth

Perimeter of Rectangle = 2 × (length + breadth)

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

Area of Square = Area of Rectangle

⇒ a² = l × b

⇒ a² = (a + 9) × (a – 6)

⇒ a² = a² – 6a + 9a – 54

⇒ 3a = 54

⇒ a = 18

⇒ l = 18 + 9 = 27 and b = 18 – 6 = 12

Perimeter of the Rectangle = 2 × (length + breadth)

Perimeter of the Rectangle = 2 × (27 + 12) = 78 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 78 cm.**

questions.question: A sum of ₹ 10000 is lent on simple interest at the rate of 15% per annum. What is the difference between Simple interest for 6 years and the simple interest for 2 years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal amount, P = 10000

Rate of interest, R = 15%

**Formula used:**

S.I = (P × N × R)/100

**Calculation:**

S.I for 6 years

S.I = (10000 × 6 × 15)/100 = 9000

S.I for 2 years

S.I = (10000 × 2 × 15)/100 = 3000

⇒ Difference between Simple interest for 6 years and the simple interest for 2 years = 9000 – 3000 = 6000

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 14 : 25. If the difference between them is 264, then which is the smaller of the two numbers?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of two numbers is 14 : 25

Difference between them is 264

**Calculation:**

Let the numbers be 14x and 25x

⇒ 25x – 14x = 264

⇒ 11x = 264

∴ x = 24

⇒ Smaller number = 14x = 14 × 24 = 336

**∴ The smaller of the two numbers is 336.**

questions.question: Average marks of 15 students of class first is 160. Average marks of 10 students of class second is 120. Average marks of 15 students of class third is 180. What will be the average marks of students of all the classes together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average marks of 15 students of class first = 160

Average marks of 10 students of class second = 120

Average marks of 15 students of class third = 180

**Formula used:**

Total marks = Average marks × Number of students

**Calculation:**

Total marks of 15 students of class first = 160 × 15 = 2400

Total marks of 10 students of class second = 120 × 10 =1200

Total marks of 15 students of class third = 180 × 15 = 2700

Total marks of students of all the classes together = 2400 + 1200 + 2700 = 6300

Total students = 15 + 10 + 15 = 40

The average marks of students of all the classes together = 6300/40 = 157.5

questions.question: Pipe X can fill a tank in 12 hours and pipe Y can fill the same tank in 36 hours. In how many hours both pipe X and pipe Y together can fill one-third part of the tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time taken by both pipes to fill the whole tank = (12 × 36) ÷ (12 + 36)

Time taken for whole tank = 432 ÷ 48 = 9 hours

To fill one-third of the tank, the time required is simply 1/3 of the total time.

Required time = 9 × (1/3) = 3 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe X to fill the tank = 12 hours

Time taken by Pipe Y to fill the tank = 36 hours

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total capacity of the tank (Total Work) = 36 units

⇒ Combined efficiency of Pipe X and Pipe Y = 3 + 1 = 4 units/hour

⇒ We need to find the time to fill one-third part of the tank.

⇒ Required work = 36 × (1/3) = 12 units

⇒ Time required = Required work ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Time required = 12 ÷ 4 = 3 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Two Pipes Filling a Tank

If pipe A fills a tank in x hours and pipe B fills it in y hours, total time taken together = (x × y) ÷ (x + y) hours.

One Filling and One Emptying Pipe

If pipe A fills in x hours and pipe B empties in y hours (where y > x), time taken to fill = (x × y) ÷ (y − x) hours.

Part of Tank Filled

To fill a specific fraction of the tank, simply multiply the total time taken to fill the entire tank by that fraction.

questions.question: The product of two numbers is 720. If their Least Common Multiple is 360, then what will be the Highest common Factor of these two numbers?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The product of two numbers = 720

Least Common Multiple = 360

**Concept:**

Product of two numbers always will be the product of their Least Common Multiple and Highest common Factor

**Formula used:**

Product of 2 numbers = LCM × HCF

**Calculation:**

720 = 360 × HCF

∴ HCF = 720/360 = 2

questions.question: A train is moving with a uniform speed. Train crosses a bridge of length 243 meters in 30 seconds and a bridge of length 343 meters in 36 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Train is moving with a uniform speed.

Train crosses a bridge of length 243 meters in 30 seconds and a bridge of length 343 meters in 36 

Seconds

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance/Time

**Calculation:**

Let the length of the train be x meter

⇒ (x + 243)/30 = (x + 343)/36

⇒ 36x + 8748 = 30x + 10290

⇒ x = 257

∴ Speed = (x + 243)/30 = (257 + 243)/30 = 16.66 meter per seconds

16.66 × (18/5) = 59.97 km/hr

⇒ From options, speed of the train = 60 km/hr

questions.question: A car covers a certain distance at a speed of 54 km/hr in 7 hours. What should be the speed of car to cover the same distance in 6 hours?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A car covers a certain distance at a speed of 54 km/hr in 7 hours

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Distance covered in 7 hours = 54 × 7 = 378 km

Speed of car to cover the same distance in 6 hours = 378/6 = 63 km/hr

(∵ Speed = Distance covered/Time taken)

questions.question: A, B and C invest ₹14000, ₹18000 and ₹24000 respectively to start a business. If the profit at the end of the year is ₹25480, then what is total share of A and B?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A, B and C invest ₹14000, ₹18000 and ₹24000 respectively

The profit at the end of the year = ₹25480

**Calculation:**

A : B : C = 14000 : 18000 : 24000 = 7 : 9 : 12

Total share of A and B = ((7 + 9)/28) × 25480 = 14560

questions.question: A person buys 25 kg of rice for Rs. 600 and sells them at a loss equal to the selling price of 5 kg rice. What will be the loss percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A person buys 25 kg of rice for ₹600

Sells them at a loss equal to the selling price of 5 kg

**Concept:**

The loss will be the same as the Selling price of 5 kg rice

**Formula used:**

Loss percentage = (Loss/ Cost Price) × 100

**Calculation:**

Cost Price of 25 kg of rice = 600

⇒ Cost Price of 1 kg of rice = 600/25 = 24

Given, Cost Price of 25 kg of rice – Selling Price of 25 kg of rice = Selling Price of 5 kg of rice

∴ Cost Price of 25 kg of rice = Selling Price of 30 kg of rice

⇒ Selling Price of 30 kg of rice = 600

⇒ Selling Price of 1 kg of rice = 600/30 = 20

**∴ Loss Percentage = ((24 – 20)/24) × 100 = 16.66%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**Loss = Cost price(CP) - Selling price(SP)

According to the question,

Loss = Selling price of 5 kg of rice

⇒ CP of 25 kg of rice – SP of 25 kg of rice = SP of 5 kg of rice

⇒ 25 CP = 30 SP

⇒ CP/SP = 30/25

Loss% = (CP - SP)×100/CP

⇒ (30 - 25)× 100/30

**⇒ 16.66%**

questions.question: A person purchases 36 articles for ₹360. How many articles must he sold for ₹360, so that the profit is 50%?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A person purchases36 articles for ₹360

**Formula used:**

Profit = S.P – C.P

Profit% = (Profit/C.P) × 100

**Calculation:**

C.P of 36 articles = 360

C.P of 1 article = 360/36 = 10

When he sold articles for 360 he got 50% profit

S.P of 1 article = 10 × (150/100) = 15

Number of articles sold = 360/15 = 24

**∴ The number of article is 24**

questions.question: 40 persons can repair a bridge in 12 days. If 8 more persons join them, then in how many days bridge can be repaired?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

40 persons can repair a bridge in 12 days

Concept:

Work = Total manpower × Total days

M1D1/W1 = M2D2/W2

**Calculation:**

M₁ = 40, D₁ = 12, M₂ = 48, D₂ = y (Let)

Using the formula

M1D1/W1 = M2D2/W2

⇒ 40 × 12 = 48 × y

⇒ y = (40 × 12/48) = 10

**∴ 48 persons can repair a bridge in 10 days.**

questions.question: The curved surface area of a cone is 550 cm². If the area of its base is 154 cm², then what will be the volume of the cone?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The curved surface area of a cone = 550 cm²

The area of its base =154 cm² 

**Formula used:**

Curved surface area of cone = πrl

Area of base = πr²

Volume of cone = (1/3) × πr²h (where r is the radius of the circle)

**Calculation:**

Area of base = πr2

⇒ πr² = 154

⇒ r = 7 cm

Curved surface area of a cone = 550 cm2

⇒ πrl = 550

⇒ l = 550/πr = 550/[(22/7) × 7] 

⇒ l = 25 cm

Now,

⇒ h = √(l)² - (r)² 

⇒ h = √ (25)² - (7)²

⇒ h = √ 576

⇒ h = 24 cm

Volume of cone = (1/3) × πr²h

⇒ V = (1/3) × (22/7) × (7²) × 24 = 1232 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1232 cm³** .
